grain_rationale: The profile shows row_count=44721 with duplicate_row_rate=0.0, so every row is a distinct physical record and none need to be collapsed. invoice_id alone has distinct_count=2330 (far below row_count), reflecting that one invoice carries many product lines, and stock_code alone has distinct_count=3141, so neither column is unique on its own; a derived identity over the ordered pair (invoice_id, stock_code) is needed to identify one invoice line event. Because duplicate_row_rate is 0.0, this identity tuple does not need to absorb exact duplicate rows, confirming a transaction grain rather than an aggregation.

fields.name: invoice_id
fields.description: The invoice number grouping line items, sampled as sequential values like 489434-489443, with null_rate 0.0 so every line is tied to an invoice.

fields.name: is_cancellation
fields.description: A boolean flag with distinct_values [false, true] and null_rate 0.0, labeling whether the invoice line represents a cancellation rather than measuring a quantity.

fields.name: stock_code
fields.description: The product code for the line, with distinct_count 3141 and null_rate 0.0, sampled as alphanumeric codes like 10002, 10002R, 10123C that label which product was sold.

fields.name: product_description
fields.description: The free-text product name such as '12 PENCIL SMALL TUBE WOODLAND'; null_rate is 0.005098 (228 nulls), so the column is nullable, likely reflecting occasional missing catalog descriptions.

fields.name: quantity
fields.description: The number of units on the line, ranging from min -1395 to max 5184 with null_rate 0.0; negative samples indicate returns or cancellations, and the value is summed/compared across lines as a measure.

fields.name: invoiced_at
fields.description: The timestamp of the invoice line, ranging from 2009-12-01T07:45:00 to 2009-12-23T16:58:00 with null_rate 0.0; samples resolve to whole minutes, so the finest usable grain is minute.

fields.name: unit_price
fields.description: The per-unit price of the product, ranging from min 0.0 to max 1998.49 with null_rate 0.0, used as a measure to compute line and invoice totals.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: An integer customer identifier ranging from 12346 to 18287; null_rate is 0.300664 (13446 nulls), nullable because many invoice lines in this retailer's data have no associated customer account (likely guest or in-store sales).

fields.name: country
fields.description: The customer's country of origin, with distinct_count 24 and null_rate 0.0, sampled as values like Australia, Austria, Belgium, France, Germany.

category_description: One row represents a single product line item on a customer invoice, identified by the combination of invoice_id and stock_code, carrying the quantity and unit price sold along with the timestamp, cancellation flag, customer, and country context for that line.
purpose: This mapping declares how the contracted silver.silver_invoice_lines table enters the gold unified event star as the invoice_lines fact category, specifying the transaction grain, the time column and its minute resolution, and the role of every profiled column; the deterministic modeling engine consumes this declaration to generate the gold fact and its dimensions.
usage: The rendered mapping contract is validated against the frozen mapping-contract schema, linted with datacontract lint, and reviewed by a human before approval; only after approval does the deterministic modeling engine read the contract to emit the gold invoice_lines fact model, so no execution happens from this proposal itself.
limitations: This mapping does not filter or exclude cancellation lines (is_cancellation=true) or negative-quantity return lines; it leaves any such business exclusion to downstream consumers. It also does not resolve the 30.07% null rate on customer_id or the 0.51% null rate on product_description, leaving null handling to consumers of the generated gold model, and it proposes no quality rules, transformations, or derived columns beyond the declared line_identity used to establish grain.
